title: Separable-closure cover and compatible finite-stage incremental coordinates
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $\Omega/k$ a separable closure [def-pd-separable-closure]. Let $I$ be the set of finite Galois intermediate fields $E/k$ (finite, normal and separable), ordered by inclusion, and put $Q_E=\operatorname{Aut}_k(E)$. Then $I$ is nonempty and directed, $\Omega=\varinjlim_{E\in I}E$, and $k\to\Omega$ is faithfully flat and ind-etale (a filtered colimit of etale algebras). The induced morphism $v:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is weakly etale and its singleton is a covering in the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For every $E\in I$ and integer $q\geq0$ the map of $\Omega$-algebras [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]
$$\theta_{E,q}:\Omega\otimes_k E^{\otimes_k q}\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{Q_E^q}\Omega,\qquad a_0\otimes\cdots\otimes a_q\longmapsto\left(a_0g_1(a_1)(g_1g_2)(a_2)\cdots(g_1\cdots g_q)(a_q)\right)_{(g_1,\ldots,g_q)}$$
is an isomorphism, with $\theta_{E,0}=1_\Omega$. If $E\subseteq E'$, the tensor inclusion on the left corresponds to precomposition of functions on the right by $Q_{E'}^q\to Q_E^q$, the componentwise restriction map.

proof.text: Finite Galois intermediate fields have bottom and binary suprema in Mathlib, hence are nonempty and directed. Every x belongs to the finite Galois field generated by {x}, so their underlying subalgebras have supremum top. Apply Subalgebra.iSupLift to a compatible family and compose with the top-subalgebra equivalence. Its inclusion formula proves compatibility; evaluating in the singleton stage proves uniqueness.

Every finitely generated subalgebra of the separable algebraic extension is a field, finite and separable over k, hence etale. Algebra.IndEtale.of_forall_fg_etale provides the filtered-colimit presentation. Apply the same argument to the canonical ULift extension to prove IndEtaleAcrossUniverses. The proved source instance makes an ind-etale algebra weakly etale, and the affine spectrum comparison supplies the scheme morphism. Both field spectra are singletons; the source is nonempty, so the map is surjective. It is quasi-compact since it is affine. The singleton criterion for propQCPrecoverage gives the small pro-etale cover. Faithful flatness follows from the nonzero free k-module structure on the field.

Construct the ordinary-label evaluation algebra map directly with PiTensorProduct.liftAlgHom and Algebra.TensorProduct.lift. Dedekind independence (Mathlib linearIndependent_monoidHom) says the embeddings a |-> sigma(a) into Omega are linearly independent. By span_flip_eq_top_iff_linearIndependent their evaluation vectors span all functions on Q. For each tensor slot j, insertion into that slot and linear closure show the range contains every function x(sigma_j). Multiplying the one-slot delta functions gives the delta function of any tuple; summing scalar multiples gives every function on Q^q, including the empty tuple for q=0.

The tensor product of q copies of a finite k-basis of E is a basis of the indexed tensor power (Basis.piTensorProduct). Base change to Omega gives a basis indexed by (Fin q -> Fin [E:k]). Thus its dimension is [E:k]^q. The function algebra has dimension |Q|^q, equal to it by the finite-Galois automorphism cardinality formula. The surjective evaluation map is therefore injective, giving the ordinary-label algebra equivalence.

The map g |-> (j |-> partialProd g (j+1)) is injective: equality of prefixes, with the zeroth prefix equal to 1, and cancellation recover every increment. It is a self-map of a finite set, so it is bijective. Precompose ordinary coordinates with this bijection. The pure-tensor formula is exactly the required ordered list-prefix product. At q=0, tensor induction and the empty indexed tensor unit formula identify the resulting map with rid composed with id tensor isEmptyEquiv.

Mathlib finGaloisGroupMap is the normal restriction homomorphism. Its defining commutation with the intermediate-field inclusion proves the one-factor evaluation identity. Being a group homomorphism, restriction preserves the product of every list prefix. Apply the pure-tensor formula and these identities, then binary and indexed tensor induction (including scalar multiples) to obtain compatibility for all tensors.
